questions.q: A hospital uses X-rays and gamma rays. (a) State one use of each [2]. (b) Explain why staff stand behind lead screens [2]. (c) Compare the frequency and speed of the two waves in a vacuum [2].
questions.a: (a) X-rays: images of bones; gamma: sterilising equipment or killing cancer cells (2); (b) ionising radiation can damage cells/cause mutations (1); lead absorbs it, reducing exposure (1); (c) gamma higher frequency (1); same speed (1)
questions.model: Teacher answers (a) aloud with the spec wording.

questions.q: Explain how infrared night-vision cameras work.
questions.a: Warm objects emit more infrared (1); the camera detects infrared and forms an image (1)

questions.q: Explain why microwaves can heat food but radio waves of the same power do not do so efficiently.
questions.a: Microwave frequencies are absorbed strongly by water molecules in food; radio waves mostly pass through.

questions.q: State one use and one danger of ultraviolet.
questions.a: Use: fluorescent lamps (or detecting forged banknotes) (1); danger: skin cancer or eye damage (1)
questions.model: Use from the spec list: fluorescent lamps. Danger: damages surface cells, so skin cancer and eye conditions.

questions.q: Put in order of increasing frequency: X-rays, microwaves, visible.
Why is gamma used to sterilise medical equipment?
questions.a: It kills microorganisms and passes through packaging
